brief: A lightweight Windows desktop reader that instantly reads selected text aloud with natural human speech when pressing Ctrl+Shift+R.
criteria: Recognizable at 16 px in Windows system tray, distinct from generic speech bubbles, evokes text selection and voice synthesis, works in monochrome and brand indigo.

concepts.name: The Soundwave Cursor
concepts.idea: A text selection caret that radiates progressive acoustic voice waves.
rationale: Unifies the two core user actions: selecting text (caret) and listening (soundwaves)
Stands out from generic chat speech bubbles
Retains crisp silhouette at 16 px and 32 px taskbar scales

concepts.name: The Acoustic S Ribbon
concepts.idea: A fluid geometric S monogram doubling as continuous sound frequency tracks.
rationale: Direct initial letter monogram (S for SpeakThat)
Fluid motion conveys real-time speech generation
Clean single-color mark reproducible in monochrome

concepts.name: The Voice Pulse Spectrum
concepts.idea: Five reader voice frequency bars centered on acoustic peak.
rationale: Pure geometric simplicity with 100/100 production readiness score
Instantly communicates audio playback and speech modulation
Extremely sharp on Windows notification area

recommendation: The Soundwave Cursor — it uniquely tells the 'select text and speak' story without falling into standard chat bubble tropes, and scales down with zero ambiguity to a 16 px tray icon.
